parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is in the presentation layer because it matches the **/*.module.ts pattern. In this layer model, NestJS modules are framework wiring files, and the file does only that job. It declares a @Global() @Module that registers one provider under the CONTEXT_STORAGE token, set to a new AsyncLocalStorage instance, and exports that token. It has no business rules, persistence, queries or request-handling logic. Creating an AsyncLocalStorage inline as a useValue is a dependency-injection binding, which is what module files are for. It does not put infrastructure behaviour in the wrong layer. The folder name __infrastructure__ differs from the presentation classification, but that comes from how the layer patterns are set up. Nothing in the file's own content belongs to another layer. No ADR prose was provided to contradict this.
